findings.title: Raw-data temp cleanup prompt lost
findings.problem: Before this change, codemie-html-report SKILL.md had an analytics-only 'Final Step — Temp file cleanup' that asked the user whether to delete the temp/ folder of raw API responses (<OUT>). Replacing html-report with the upstream copy removed that step. The rewritten codemie-analytics Step 3a hand-off (and the deleted Step 3b) does not restore it, and SKILL.md:183 still says temp files are not cleaned up automatically.
findings.impact: Analytics runs now leave raw API responses on disk with no prompt to delete them. These can hold per-user spending and leaderboard data. This is a behaviour regression introduced by this change, confirmed by reading the old html-report SKILL.md at 916710fb and the current analytics hand-off.
findings.recommendation: Decide where the analytics-only "ask the user whether to delete temp/ (<OUT>)" step now lives. The likely place is a final step after the Step 3a hand-off in codemie-analytics/SKILL.md, because html-report must stay byte-identical to upstream. This needs a human scope call, because the spec allows no analytics edits beyond the hand-off.

findings.title: No check that the commonjs pin ships
findings.problem: This is a regression gap. The skill scripts load only because the new nested package.json {"type":"commonjs"} overrides the root "type":"module". No test or gate spawns any skill script from src/ or dist/, and shipping relies only on copy-plugins.js:25 not filtering .json files.
findings.impact: If the one-line package.json is dropped, renamed or excluded from what ships, every build.js and inject-*.js call fails at load time with 'require is not defined in ES module scope'. Reports and decks then cannot be built. AC9 checks this once in Stage 7, but nothing guards it afterwards. Consumer: the build step that the codemie-html-report SKILL.md tells the agent to run.
findings.recommendation: Decide whether to add a lasting guard, such as a post-build check or a test that spawns `dist/.../codemie-html-report/scripts/build.js` on a fixture and expects exit 0. Without the nested package.json, every CommonJS script fails to load. AGENTS.md allows tests only on explicit request, and the stand-in chose hands-on validation (AC9) instead of a test, so this needs the user's explicit go-ahead.

findings.title: CommonJS skill scripts break the Imports rule
findings.problem: code-quality.md's Imports rule requires ES modules with no require()/CommonJS, and AGENTS.md Common Pitfalls says to avoid require() and __dirname. build.js, inject-charts.js, inject-controls.js, inject-css.js and inject-data.js use both, and this change opts the skill into CommonJS with a new package.json {"type":"commonjs"}. The spec chose the pin over an ESM rewrite, but in an autonomous spec gate (product-owner stand-in SR-001), not as a user decision.
findings.impact: The repo's documented code-quality standard is not met by newly shipped scripts. The rule and the spec's copy-verbatim choice cannot both hold without a recorded exemption.
findings.recommendation: Get a human decision. One option is to convert build.js and the inject-*.js scripts to ES modules (`import` from 'node:...', directory from `import.meta.url`) and drop the `{"type":"commonjs"}` pin. That diverges from upstream. The other option is to document in code-quality.md that vendored skill scripts under `claude/plugin/skills` are exempt. The spec chose the pin, but a stand-in agent made that choice, not the user.

findings.title: Duplicated 1956-line slop-scan without drift guard
findings.problem: code-quality.md's Code Structure Guidelines keep files under 500 lines. slop-scan.mjs is 1956 lines and ships byte-identical in codemie-html-report and codemie-humanizer, as does references/glossary.md. No test or gate checks that the copies stay identical; the spec's cmp is a one-off validation step. The READMEs also cite a drift-guard test (evals/humanizer-shared-files.test.ts) that does not exist in this repo.
findings.impact: A fix to one scanner's rules leaves the other skill grading text differently, so the html-report build gate and codemie-humanizer can disagree about the same text without any failure. This is also a documented structure standard that is not met.
findings.recommendation: Get a human decision. Options: ship one shared copy if the plugin layout allows it, add a gate or test that checks the two slop-scan.mjs and glossary.md copies are identical, or mark slop-scan.mjs as vendored and exempt from the 500-line structure rule. The `cmp` run during validation is a one-off check, not a guard.
findings.check_notes: Mapped hitl decision: vitest byte-identity drift guard; file length accepted; command exit 0
